name: Loeys-Dietz Syndrome

diagnosticCriteria.formalCriteriaName: No formal consensus criteria; diagnosis based on clinical features plus genetic confirmation

criteria.description: Arterial tortuosity and/or aneurysm (especially aortic root)
Pathogenic variant in TGFBR1, TGFBR2, SMAD3, TGFB2, or TGFB3
Thin translucent skin with visible veins
Easy bruising and poor wound healing
Allergic/atopic disease (eosinophilic GI disease, asthma, food allergy)

diagnosticCriteria.minimumForDiagnosis: Genetic confirmation of a pathogenic variant in a TGF-beta signaling pathway gene (TGFBR1, TGFBR2, SMAD3, TGFB2, TGFB3) plus compatible clinical features.
diagnosticCriteria.notes: Five subtypes based on causative gene (LDS Types 1-5). Aortic events can occur at smaller diameters than in Marfan syndrome.

pathognomonic.symptomName: Triad of arterial tortuosity/aneurysm, hypertelorism, and bifid uvula/cleft palate
pathognomonic.notes: Classic triad; not all three features present in every patient

common.notes: Can dissect at smaller diameters than Marfan

occasional.symptomName: Eosinophilic gastrointestinal disease or food allergies
occasional.notes: More common in TGFB2 and TGFB3 subtypes

rare.notes: More associated with SMAD3 variants (LDS Type 3)

laboratory: Elevated IgE or eosinophilia in some subtypes
imaging: CT or MR angiography from head to pelvis for full arterial assessment
Arterial tortuosity visible on angiographic imaging
genetic: SMAD3 mutations (LDS Type 3, a.k.a. Aneurysms-Osteoarthritis Syndrome)
other: Surgical thresholds may be lower than Marfan (aortic root >= 4.0-4.2 cm in adults)

distinguishingFeatures: Marfan has ectopia lentis (absent in LDS)
Marfan lacks bifid uvula and hypertelorism
Marfan usually dissects at larger aortic diameters
vEDS involves medium-artery rupture more than aortic root dilation
vEDS has characteristic facial features different from LDS
vEDS lacks hypertelorism and bifid uvula

redFlags: Rapid aortic root growth or diameter approaching surgical threshold
Acute chest, back, or abdominal pain (suspect dissection or rupture)
Arterial aneurysms in multiple vascular territories
references: Loeys BL, et al. A syndrome of altered cardiovascular, craniofacial, neurocognitive and skeletal development caused by mutations in TGFBR1 or TGFBR2. Nat Genet. 2005;37(3):275-81.
MacCarrick G, et al. Loeys-Dietz syndrome: a primer for diagnosis and management. Genet Med. 2014;16(8):576-87.
Meester JAN, et al. Differences in manifestations of Marfan syndrome, Ehlers-Danlos syndrome, and Loeys-Dietz syndrome. Ann Cardiothorac Surg. 2017;6(6):582-94.
